title: Ashi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: At the beginning of [Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.1.18), Rav Chisda transmits in Ashi’s name. Hyman argues that the reading should in fact be Assi: this is Rav Assi, who is almost always called by this name in the Jerusalem Talmud.
Rav Acha son of Rav Ashi, [Zevachim 91a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.91a.17). (But Hyman says that there the text should read "son of Rava.")
Rav Chama bar Ashi, [Yerushalmi Ketubot 2:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.2.9.4). Chanin bar Ashi, [Bekhorot 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.34a.8).
Rav Yitzchak bar Ashi, [Pesachim 45b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.45b.9-11). Mar bar Rav Ashi, [Berakhot 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.36a.22).
Rav Mari son of Rav Ashi, [Bava Metzia 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.103a.7).
Rav Sama son of Rav Ashi, [Ketubot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33b.1).[^3]

notes.text: The citation is the beginning of Shabbat, chapter 1, folio 2b, not folio 281. The checked Jerusalem Talmud chapter contains both Ashi and Assi; changing Ashi to Assi remains Hyman’s emendation.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:1 has Chisda in Ashi’s name and, in a separate paragraph, Chisda in Assi’s name. These occurrences do not themselves authorize harmonizing Ashi to Assi. The emendation, near-universal naming assertion and Zevachim son-of-Rava correction remain Hyman’s claims.

The two Yerushalmi Shabbat passages preserve Ashi and Assi with different formulations. Yerushalmi Ketubot distinguishes Rav Chiyya bar Ashi from Rav Chama bar Ashi in successive reports. Ketubot 33b gives Rav Sama son of Rav Assi or, alternatively, son of Rav Ashi. See also [Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:1 (the Assi passage)](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.1.26).
